slot.brief: Rank the van 't Hoff factors of a sugar solution and two electrolytes of different stoichiometry (e.g. 1:1 vs 2:1 salts) in water; test the i = number of ions idea.

stem: In dilute water, assuming complete dissociation of the electrolytes, what is the increasing order of van ’t Hoff factors for glucose, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CaCl}_2$?

verdicts.working: Glucose does not dissociate (i = 1); NaCl gives 2 ions (i = 2); CaCl₂ gives 3 ions (i = 3).

working:
Glucose: $i=1$; $\text{NaCl}\rightarrow 2$ ions, so $i=2$; $\text{CaCl}_2\rightarrow 3$ ions, so $i=3$.

Independent check: Glucose does not dissociate (i = 1); NaCl gives 2 ions (i = 2); CaCl₂ gives 3 ions (i = 3).
solution: For complete dissociation, the van ’t Hoff factor equals the number of particles formed per formula unit. Glucose: $i=1$; NaCl: $i=2$; CaCl$_2$: $i=3$. Hence, $\text{glucose}<\text{NaCl}<\text{CaCl}_2$.
